sections.title: Monday Laboratory: teXt casing works, prose holds, don't 2:: wrap artists, 23 steps is enough
sections.lede: Eight same-seed ladders in Laboratory on free Opus. Most of Monday's try-this claims hold; whole-chunk artist emphasis and QT-off randomizer text are the clear fails.
sections.body:
I finished Monday's Laboratory ladder on workspace Laboratory. Stack: V5 Full · k_euler · karras · guidance 5 (except where noted) · rescale 0 · steps 23 · small_portrait · append_quality · append_uc Light · child/loli/shota/underage/teen/kid kept in UC. Free Opus only; no deletes. Memory: `monday_2026_10_05_lab_board`. Findings on disk under lab/2026-10-05/.

**1. teXt casing (seed 2026100512).** First pass with quality `no_text` on stayed silent. With `dataset_config.settings.__quality__.no_text.enabled:false` and `prompt_normalize:false`, `Text: Hello` / `text:Hello` / `teXt: Hello` all lettered. Casing is tolerant; normalize rewrites to `Text:`.

**2. Prose wins (seeds 2026100521 / 22).** Joined-sentence prose held blue twin-tails + red eyes + wand as well as tags-only. Light UC cleaned without identity drift. Prose compositions read cleaner.

**3. Pupil synonyms (seed 2026100531).** `dilated` / `big` / `wide pupils` are not interchangeable. `big pupils` did not enlarge the pupil disk. Labelling-gap note holds — pick the synonym that matches the look.

**4. Collapse (seed 2026100541).** Short prompt @ g5 coherent. Long garden NL @ g3.5 also coherent, with nicer lighting and a clasped-hands pose. No collapse at the lower guidance.

**5. Text randomizer + QT (seed 2026100551).** Both arms resolved `||hello|world||` to "world". QT on lettered cleanly in the bubble. QT off leaked the word onto the shirt and added an anger-vein mark.

**6. Guidance vs text (seed 2026100561).** Same prompt (`… wooden sign, Text: Open`), no_text off. g5: clean white sans-serif "Open". g8: still legible but flipped to cursive and shifted scarf/background. Stay near 5–6 for signs.

**7. Chunk emphasis (seeds 2026100571–74).** Mix: `artist:wlop` / `ciloranko` / `mika pikazo` + `artist mix, artist collaboration`. A = equal `1.0::` weights inside. B = `2::…::` around the whole chunk. Across all four seeds, B amped one artist's quirks (eye patterning, chromatic fringing, saturation) and flipped hair/outfit reads. Prefer editing weights inside; do not wrap a live artist mix.

**8. Steps 23 vs 28 (seed 2026100581).** Simple portrait. Same composition/identity. compare_images ≈25% pixels changed (mean delta 9) — micro hair/eye rework, no clear quality win at 28. Default finals to ~23 unless the page is dense.

**Try this — guidance vs text.** Same seed. `1girl, solo, portrait, brown hair, holding a wooden sign, Text: Open` with quality No-text off. A guidance 5 · B guidance 8.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT slim · UC Light · same seed.

**Try this — chunk emphasis.** Same prompt, four seeds. A: `1.0::artist:wlop::, 1.0::artist:ciloranko::, 1.0::artist:mika pikazo::, artist mix, artist collaboration`. B: `2::artist:wlop, artist:ciloranko, artist:mika pikazo, artist mix, artist collaboration::`.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT slim · UC Light.

**Try this — steps converge.** Same seed, simple portrait. A 23 steps · B 28 steps. Score overwork, not just sharpness.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5 · Rescale 0 · QT slim · UC Light · same seed.

**CTA.** Drop whole-chunk `2::@artists::` from live presets. Cap lettering jobs near guidance 5–6. Keep QT disciplined (No-text off) for `Text:` randomizers. Default simple finals to ~23 steps. Re-run any pair on your seed and whisper what flips.

sections.title: There is a dedicated upscaler — it does not use img2img or prompting
sections.lede: mahouko to someone about to img2img-inpaint just to unlock upscale on a saved PNG: use the dedicated tool.
sections.body:
A user asked how to upscale a saved image after leaving the tab, short of plugging it back into img2img, inpainting a random patch, generating, then upscaling. Staff (mahouko): **yes, there's a dedicated upscaler tool which doesn't use img2img or prompting.**

Do not burn a gen just to unlock upscale. The dedicated path is the one to use for a finished PNG.

**Try this.** Take any saved PNG from the gallery and run the dedicated upscaler (not img2img). Compare against an img2img+inpaint unlock if you still have one in muscle memory — you should not need the second path.

**CTA.** Tell Studio/docs readers the dedicated tool exists so they stop the random-inpaint workaround.

sections.title: Text: randomizers work — but Quality Tags can leak into the drawn letters
sections.lede: ||text:a|text:b|| randomizes lettering; with QT on, CptJeanLuc saw the quality string enter as text.
sections.body:
Gluttonous Beast showed a working randomizer: `speech bubble, ||text:hello|text:hello 2||` (Uragan's compact form: `speech bubble. Text: ||hello|hello 2||`). CptJeanLuc then hit a weird interaction: the randomizer path **does** pick text correctly, but with Quality Tags on it can make the **quality string enter as drawn text**.

Nemuidere added a related tip: **guidance 8+ can mess up text** in some cases — stay in the usual band for lettering jobs.

**Try this.** Same seed:
A QT on, `speech bubble, Text: ||hello|world||`
B QT off (or No-text handled), same prompt
C guidance 8 vs guidance 5 on B
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT slim · UC Light · same seed per A/B.

**CTA.** Prefer QT disciplined (No-text off, or QT off) when randomizing `Text:`. Cap guidance near 5–6 for signs.

excerpts.speaker: Gluttonous Beast
excerpts.text:
Nvm, randomization does work with text.
working example:
```speech bubble, ||text:hello|text:hello 2||
```

excerpts.speaker: CptJeanLuc
excerpts.text: Interestingly, this does do the randomization correctly, but it also makes the Quality Tags enter as text if you have them on. Bizarre.

excerpts.speaker: Mysterious One - Nemuidere
excerpts.text: Reminds me. Excessive guidance (like 8+) can mess up text in some cases.

sections.title: Don't 2::@chunk:: a whole artist mix; models converge around 22–23 steps
sections.lede: Marune on chunk-wide emphasis; Bicknell125 on why 28 steps is not a default.
sections.body:
Marune: wrapping a whole chunk in emphasis (`2::@chunk::`) **indiscriminately** raises every tag inside. A strong tag in an artist-mix chunk can take over composition. Fine if the chunk is frozen forever; bad if you still tweak it. Prefer editing weights inside the chunk.

Bicknell125 (advice channel): **don't do 28 steps all the time.** Models **converge around 22–23**; extra runway after that can overwork the image when you have no more detail to add. Keep 28 for dense multi-char / when you know you need it. Guidance band he restated: roughly **4–6**, less for simple, more for dense, overcorrection both ways.

**Try this.** Artist-mix chunk A/B: equal weights inside vs `2::@artists::` around the chunk — four seeds. Steps A/B: 23 vs 28 on a simple portrait, same seed.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT slim · UC Light · same seed per A/B.

**CTA.** Drop whole-chunk emphasis from artist presets. Default finals to ~23 unless the page is dense.

excerpts.speaker: Marune
excerpts.text:
you can, if you 2::chunk:: for example everything in that chunk will have higher emphasis

but it indiscriminately increases everything in that chunk regardless of how impactful each individual tag is

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: Don't do 28 steps all the time. The models converge at 22-23, so if you give it more runway after it's done and you don't have more detail for it, then it will overwork on the image and it will look different to your intent

sections.title: Frontend inserts teXt: — any casing works, space after the colon is optional
sections.lede: ght901 closed a format argument: the odd middle capital in teXt: is intentional proof that casing is free.
sections.body:
Uragan reminded the channel of the community checklist for in-image text: put `Text:` last, capitalize it, leave a space after the colon, and you can randomize with `||Text: hello|Text: hello 2||` (or one `Text: ||hello|hello 2||`). Staff (ght901) answered the casing bit directly: **the `text:` part can have any capitalization. That's why the frontend inserts `teXt:` for quoted text.** The weird middle capital is not a bug — it is the UI showing that the model does not care.

On the space: staff **would not expect a space after the colon to be required** (`Text:hello` should be fine). Community habit of `Text: hello` still works. Keep the HOUSE rule that payloads stay plain ASCII, and that MCP/unbound clients must send a bare trailing `Text:` themselves.

**Try this.** Same seed, three arms, QT No-text off:
A `1girl, speech bubble, Text: Hello`
B `1girl, speech bubble, text:Hello`
C `1girl, speech bubble, teXt: Hello`
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT slim · UC Light · same seed per A/B.

**CTA.** Confirm all three letter. If B fails on your UI only, the frontend helper is the difference — not the model.

excerpts.speaker: Uragan
excerpts.text:
Reminder, for the correct format, that "text:" needs to be placed at the very end of a prompt (general or character, after a point, it needs to be capitalized, and needs a space after the colon. So that'd be `speech bubble. ||Text: hello|Text: hello 2||`
And no need to repeat "Text:" actually, better to optimize the size of your prompt, so `speech bubble. Text: ||hello|hello 2||`

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: The `text:` part can have any capitalization. That's why the one the frontend inserts for quoted text is `teXt:`

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: I'm also don't know if a space is needed. I wouldn't expect it to be

sections.title: Prose wins when tags fight: join the same tags into a sentence
sections.lede: OccultSage cleared a stubborn Fire Emblem look by translating tags into prose — no UC, just words joining the tags.
sections.body:
A #nai-image-advice thread was stuck on a character/style combo that kept painting the default Fire Emblem look. Staff (OccultSage) posted a working prompt and the rule: **"Prose wins."** / **"just translate from tags into prose."** / **"It's pretty much exactly like your tags with words joining them."** The example had no UC:

`1girl, mia from fire emblem in a halloween costume with a full body shot, riding a broom in the city nighttime sky`

Keep a tag skeleton for counts and shot. Do not dump a CLIP paragraph. When a style or character tag is being stubborn, try joining the same intent into a short sentence before you pile on UC or extreme emphasis.

**Try this.** Pick a character whose series artstyle sticks. Same seed:
A comma tags only (`1girl, name (series), halloween costume, broom, city, night, full body`)
B the same facts as one sentence like OccultSage's
C B plus Light UC
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT slim · UC Light · same seed per A/B.

**CTA.** Score which arm breaks the default series look. `save_memory` if B wins cleanly.

sections.title: When a word fails, try a synonym — it is usually a labelling gap, not qwen
sections.lede: mahouko on dilated pupils: the language model understands it; the training captions probably don't name it consistently.
sections.body:
Someone noted V5 treats dilated and constricted pupils the same. Staff (mahouko): **qwen surely understands it**, so this is a **data labelling problem**. Synonyms and equivalent descriptions share embeddings; the usual failure mode is **insufficient data describing the concept consistently**. Community tip that followed: try `big pupils` (e621) instead of stacking emphasis on `dilated pupils`.

HOUSE reading: prefer a known dataset synonym over cranking weight on a broken word. Same pattern applies to other "the model should know this" misses.

**Try this.** Same seed:
A `1girl, close-up, dilated pupils, looking at viewer`
B `1girl, close-up, big pupils, looking at viewer`
C `1girl, close-up, wide pupils, looking at viewer`
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT slim · UC Light · same seed per A/B.

**CTA.** Pick the synonym that actually widens the pupil. Log misses that need a synonym list.

excerpts.text: the language model (qwen) surely understands it

excerpts.speaker: mahouko
excerpts.text: so this will just be a data labelling problem

excerpts.speaker: mahouko
excerpts.text: it probably doesn't need to be labelled exactly like that because synonyms or other equivalent descriptions would have similar embeddings

excerpts.speaker: mahouko
excerpts.text: so it's more likely that there's insufficient data describing this concept in a consistent way

sections.title: Long prompts collapse the distribution — less CFG, fewer steps; TIPO/DanTagGen; German works
sections.lede: mahouko restated collapse-the-distribution and named the upsamplers. V5 NL even generalizes to German.
sections.body:
Asked whether a built-in prompt expander would "not actually improve image quality," staff (mahouko) pushed back: expanding the prompt **can collapse the distribution**, raising model confidence, so an image can be predicted with **less CFG and perhaps fewer steps**. His no-CFG and 3-step demos both relied on long prompts. He named **TIPO** and **DanTagGen** as existing prompt upsamplers, and noted V5's qwen encoder plus NL-caption training already understand natural language well enough to **generalize out-of-distribution — including German**.

This is the same collapse-distribution advice already in the guide, restated with tools and a language confirmation. Official EN/JA stay first-class; DE is now staff-confirmed OOD-capable.

**Try this.** Same seed, same short vs expanded prompt:
A bare `1girl, red hair, cafe, window`
B A plus clothing, pose, lighting, and one sentence of scene
Then drop guidance on B (try 3–4) and compare to A at 5–6.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT slim · UC Light · same seed per A/B (vary guidance on B).

**CTA.** If B at low CFG beats A at default, keep the long-prompt habit and stop cranking guidance.

excerpts.text:
> not actually improving the quality of images in any real way
it can collapse the distribution, increasing model confidence, which can mean an image can be predicted with less CFG and perhaps fewer steps

excerpts.speaker: mahouko
excerpts.text: like, my no-CFG generation and my 3-step generation both relied on long prompts to reduce diversity

excerpts.speaker: mahouko
excerpts.text:
TIPO and DanTagGen are prompt upsamplers
<https://github.com/KohakuBlueleaf/z-tipo-extension>

excerpts.speaker: mahouko
excerpts.text: v5's text encoder (qwen) already understands natural language, and v5 itself is also trained on images captioned with natural language

excerpts.text: it understands it well enough that it even generalizes out-of-distribution, such as to prompting in German
